reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Remonstrances and hearing of witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1949 p. 551 § 8475a, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070). Covers the remonstrance threshold (signed by 12+ municipal township residents, 3+ in the immediate neighborhood; retaining source phrasing "three of whom which reside") and the county commission duty to hear parties' witnesses on public necessity, practicability, probable landowner damages, and establishment/building expenses including bridges and culverts.

headings.title: Commission findings, dismissal, and establishment orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers county commission disposition after the subsection 1 hearing: dismissal if facts do not justify establishing the road, or an order establishing the road at county, petitioner, or shared expense if justified.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of both subsections and history note (L. 1949 p. 551 § 8475a, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked remonstrance signature thresholds, retained verbatim source phrasing ('three of whom which reside'), and verified witness-hearing scope and dismissal versus establishment-order outcomes; both drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Vacation petitions, initial reading, and continuance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior revisions, cross-references (71.250–71.280, 229.420–229.450, 214.060–214.070), and case annotations (Burrows, Corbin, State v. Herman). Covers application by 12 township residents to vacate a road or part thereof as useless and an unreasonable repair burden, initial public reading on the first day of the term, and mandatory continuance to the next term.

headings.title: Posted notice, personal service, and second reading
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers posting notice in at least three public places in the township(s) at least 20 days before the next term, personal service on district residents whose lands are crossed or touched, and second public reading on the first day of the next regular term.

headings.title: Remonstrances, vacation orders, costs, and reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes. Covers permissive vacation at petitioners' cost when no written remonstrance by 12+ township residents is filed, shifting costs to remonstrators if vacation is found just over a remonstrance, and petitioner reimbursement of original opening costs and damages unless five years have elapsed since original opening.

headings.title: Charter county road vacation petitions and procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes (including A.L. 2007 S.B. 22). Covers the notwithstanding-clause procedure for charter counties allowing 25+ county residents on the road or an intersecting road within one mile of the right-of-way to apply for vacation as no longer serving public health, safety, and welfare, and local authority to set notice, hearing, and remonstrance procedures by order or ordinance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections, history/prior revisions (through A.L. 2007 S.B. 22), cross-references (71.250-71.280, 229.420-229.450, 214.060-214.070), and case annotations (Burrows, Corbin, State v. Herman), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 12-resident township petition/reading/continuance steps, posted/personal notice, remonstrance cost-shifting and five-year reimbursement exception, and charter-county 25-resident notwithstanding procedure; all four drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Requested stenographic record at party expense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1949 p. 551 § 8477), and case annotations (Elrod, Ross). Covers making a stenographic record of county commission proceedings to establish or vacate a public road, conditional on request and payment by petitioners or remonstrators.

headings.title: Judicial review of orders under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes, including Elrod (review under § 536.110) and Ross (§ 49.230 does not impliedly repeal § 228.120). Preserves the exact chapter 536 cross-reference for judicial review of county commission orders establishing or vacating a public road.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history note (L. 1949 p. 551 § 8477), and case annotations (Elrod, Ross), and verified all fingerprints. Checked the party-request and party-expense conditions for stenographic records and preserved the exact chapter 536 judicial-review cross-reference; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: County-line road authority, minimum width, and shared costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8479). Covers county commission authority to establish county-boundary highways as provided in sections 228.020 to 228.130, the 40-foot minimum width, and equal half-cost sharing between counties for establishment and repair.

headings.title: Joint commission proceedings, filings, and hearing schedules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers venue in any concerned county, sitting as one joint commission with majority rule in the originating county, filing and recording certified final judgments and county highway engineer reports in each county, and non-interfering hearing schedules.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8479) and verified all fingerprints. Checked sections 228.020 to 228.130 reference, 40-foot minimum width, equal half-cost sharing, joint-commission majority proceedings in the originating county, certified judgment/engineer report filings, and hearing scheduling; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Districting and repair of newly opened roads
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8480), and cross-reference (61.071). Covers districting and repairing newly opened roads in the same manner as other public roads.

headings.title: Possession timing, fence and crop allowances, and refusal penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers county commission or circuit court judgment specifying when the owner must yield possession, allowing reasonable time up to six months for fences plus time to gather growing crops, and treating failure or refusal to open on time as punishable highway obstruction. Independent review revised title from 'Possession deadlines, fence and crop allowances, and penalties' to avoid pluralizing the single court-specified time and highway-obstruction refusal penalty.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8480), and cross-reference (61.071), and verified all fingerprints. Checked newly opened road districting/repair and judgment timing with fence (up to six months) and growing-crop allowances plus highway-obstruction refusal penalty. Retained subsection 1 title; revised subsection 2 title to 'Possession timing, fence and crop allowances, and refusal penalty'.

headings.title: County eminent domain for road property and materials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8486, A.L. 1983 S.B. 44 & 45, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070), and case annotations (Everett on quarry stone use; County of Greene v. Hammons on supersession/implied repeal of contrary judicial-phase provisions by §§ 49.300 and 228.100). Describes archived text vesting eminent domain in counties for road land, earth, stone, timber, quarries, gravel pits, bridges, abutments, and fills without asserting current enforceability. Independent review revised title from 'County eminent domain authority for road property' to explicitly reflect road materials (earth, stone, timber, rock quarries, gravel pits) alongside land and structures.

headings.title: Necessity orders, engineer surveys, and published notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes (including County of Greene v. Hammons supersession annotation). Covers the county commission public-necessity order of record, 15-day directive for county highway engineer survey/map/report filed with county clerk, and three-week consecutive newspaper publication notice.

headings.title: Filing and commission hearing of damage claims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes (including County of Greene v. Hammons supersession annotation). Covers permissive filing of damage claims with the county clerk by owners or conservators of disabled persons or minors within 20 days after last publication, and county commission hearing at the next regular or adjourned term.

headings.title: Circuit court transfer, hearing scheduling, and service
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes, explicitly retaining the 1965 County of Greene v. Hammons annotation that §§ 49.300 and 228.100 supersede and impliedly repeal contrary judicial-phase provisions. Describes archived text covering transfer to circuit court upon disagreement or non-filing, 30-day hearing order, and 10-day service on owners and conservators.

headings.title: Six-juror panel, property view, and damages verdict
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and section notes, explicitly retaining the 1965 County of Greene v. Hammons supersession/implied-repeal annotation. Describes archived text on impaneling six disinterested resident jurors, viewing property, determining damages, five-juror verdict concurrence, and impaneling another jury on disagreement.

headings.title: Limits on necessity inquiry and appellate review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and section notes, explicitly retaining the 1965 County of Greene v. Hammons annotation that §§ 49.300 and 228.100 supersede and impliedly repeal contrary judicial-phase provisions. Neutrally describes the archived text barring circuit court inquiry into public necessity and barring appellate or writ-of-error review without claiming current enforceability.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections, history/prior revisions (through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070), and case annotations (Everett on quarry stone; 1965 County of Greene v. Hammons holding §§ 49.300 and 228.100 supersede and impliedly repeal contrary judicial-phase provisions), and verified all fingerprints. Ensured neutral topic labels describing the archived text without claiming current enforceability of superseded judicial-phase procedures; revised subsection 1 title to 'County eminent domain for road property and materials' and retained subsections 2-6.

headings.title: Legal establishment and abandonment by nonuse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8485 through A.L. 2007 S.B. 22), and all 16 case annotations (1952–2005 on prescriptive use, public funds/labor, abandonment, platted streets, width, and dedication). Covers legal establishment by county commission order plus 10-year public use or 10-year continuous public use with public money/labor, and abandonment/vacation by 5 years continuous public nonuse. Independent review revised title from 'Establishment by order or use and abandonment' to remove grouping ambiguity, avoid implying public use alone without public money/labor suffices, and specify nonuse abandonment.

headings.title: County aid road trust fund roads and vacation limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers conclusive public county road status from and after January 1, 1990 for roads identified as county roads receiving county aid road trust funds from or through the department of transportation for at least five years, and restricting abandonment/vacation to county commission public-hearing action or section 228.110 procedures. Independent review revised title from 'County aid trust fund roads and vacation limits' to match the exact statutory fund name ('county aid road trust funds').

headings.title: Location proof in litigation and court-ordered surveys
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes. Covers dispensing with proof of exact location in litigation under this section and permissive judicial authority, once road existence is determined, to order a location survey and charge survey costs to the party asserting road existence.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, history/prior revisions (through A.L. 2007 S.B. 22), and all 16 case annotations (1952-2005), and verified all fingerprints. Checked 10-year order/use and public-money/labor requirements, five-year nonuse abandonment, January 1, 1990 CART-fund conclusive status and § 228.110 vacation limits, and permissive court-ordered location surveys. Revised subsection 1 to 'Legal establishment and abandonment by nonuse' and subsection 2 to 'County aid road trust fund roads and vacation limits'; retained subsection 3.

headings.title: Circuit court petitions for private road maintenance plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2012 H.B. 1103). Covers permissive circuit court petition by one or more benefitted homeowners (abutting owners or easement holders) for a private road used by more than one homeowner, conditional on absence of a prior order or written agreement (including deed covenants or permits) and inability to agree in writing on a plan and cost apportionment.

headings.title: Apportionment of maintenance plan costs among owners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers apportioning private road maintenance plan costs among abutting residence owners and easement holders commensurate with use and benefit, by mutual agreement or court order using listed non-exclusive methods (equal division, residential assessed value, front footage, or usage/benefit).

headings.title: Court procedures and appointment of disinterested commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive court use of chapter 228 private-road establishment/widening procedures to order and determine a maintenance plan, including appointing and compensating disinterested commissioners.

headings.title: Designation and compensation of a maintenance supervisor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers court-appointed commissioners designating a supervisor to complete the maintenance plan when benefitted homeowners cannot agree, with compensation in the same manner as commissioners.

headings.title: Recording maintenance agreements and final court orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers mandatory recording with the county recorder of deeds of any maintenance plan agreement executed by all homeowners or final court order approving a plan.

headings.title: Enforcement actions by adjoining homeowners or easement holders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers permissive standing for one or more adjoining homeowners or easement holders to sue to enforce either a mutually agreed or court-ordered private road maintenance plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections and history note (L. 2012 H.B. 1103) and verified all fingerprints. Checked multi-homeowner private road triggers, absence-of-prior-order/agreement condition, cost apportionment among abutting owners and easement holders, chapter 228 procedures/commissioners, supervisor designation when homeowners disagree, mandatory recording, and permissive enforcement actions; all six drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Amendment or restatement by unanimous recorded agreement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2012 H.B. 1103). Covers amending, modifying, or restating a prior maintenance agreement or court order at any time by recorded agreement signed by all homeowners or other benefitted owners.

headings.title: Seven-year waiting period and exceptions for court modification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the seven-year bar on filing a section 228.369 court proceeding to amend, modify, or restate a plan after a prior order, qualified by prima facie exceptions for property development/division rendering the plan obsolete or existing use-and-benefit apportionment becoming inequitable.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 2012 H.B. 1103) and verified all fingerprints. Checked unanimous recorded amendment/restatement authority and the seven-year bar on section 228.369 court modification filings with its two prima facie exceptions; both drafted titles retained.
